from datetime import date

from late_fee import LateFeeCalculator


def test_grace_period_returns_zero():
    calculator = LateFeeCalculator(today=date(2024, 1, 15))

    assert calculator.compute_fee_cents(100_000, date(2024, 1, 1)) == 0


def test_minimum_fee_applies_after_grace_period():
    calculator = LateFeeCalculator(today=date(2024, 1, 16))

    assert calculator.compute_fee_cents(10_000, date(2024, 1, 1)) == 500


def test_maximum_fee_is_capped_at_25_percent_of_original_balance():
    calculator = LateFeeCalculator(today=date(2024, 4, 30))

    assert calculator.compute_fee_cents(10_000, date(2024, 1, 1)) == 2_500


def test_weekends_are_excluded_from_days_past_due():
    calculator = LateFeeCalculator(today=date(2024, 1, 16))

    # Jan 1 through Jan 16 contains 11 weekdays, so only 1 day is billable.
    # A weekend-inclusive calculation would produce a larger fee.
    assert calculator.compute_fee_cents(1_000_000, date(2024, 1, 1)) == 500


def test_fee_is_rounded_to_whole_cents_half_up():
    calculator = LateFeeCalculator(today=date(2024, 1, 16))

    # One billable weekday:
    # 1,001,000 * (0.015 / 30) = 500.5 cents -> 501 cents.
    assert calculator.compute_fee_cents(1_001_000, date(2024, 1, 1)) == 501


def test_returns_zero_when_balance_is_non_positive():
    calculator = LateFeeCalculator(today=date(2024, 4, 30))

    assert calculator.compute_fee_cents(0, date(2024, 1, 1)) == 0
    assert calculator.compute_fee_cents(-100, date(2024, 1, 1)) == 0


def test_today_can_be_injected_for_deterministic_calculation():
    calculator = LateFeeCalculator(today=date(2024, 1, 1))

    # Injected today is on the due date, so no weekdays have elapsed.
    assert calculator.compute_fee_cents(100_000, date(2024, 1, 1)) == 0
